title: GCP Security Overview
content: Security in Google Cloud is a shared responsibility. Google secures the underlying infrastructure, while you are responsible for securing your data and applications within the cloud.
insight: Understanding the shared responsibility model is fundamental to cloud security.

title: IAM Policy Structure
content: An IAM policy is a collection of bindings. A binding binds one or more members to a single role. A member can be a user, group, domain, or service account.
insight: Policies are hierarchical and are inherited from higher levels (Org -> Folder -> Project).

lab.command: echo 'IAM policies are represented in JSON or YAML format'
lab.output: IAM policies are represented in JSON or YAML format

title: IAM Conditions
content: IAM Conditions allow you to grant access to resources only if specific conditions are met, such as the request's timing or the resource's attributes.
insight: Conditions add an extra layer of context-aware security to your IAM policies.

lab.command: echo 'Configure conditions in the Console or via gcloud with --condition'
lab.output: Configure conditions in the Console or via gcloud with --condition

title: Predefined Roles
content: Predefined roles are created and maintained by Google. They provide granular access to specific services and are updated as new permissions are added.
insight: Always prefer predefined roles over basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) for better granularity.

lab.output:
--- 
name: roles/storage.objectAdmin
title: Storage Object Admin

title: Custom Roles
content: Custom roles allow you to define a specific set of permissions. Use them when predefined roles don't match your requirements.
insight: Custom roles are maintained by you and only exist within the project or organization where they were created.

title: Service Accounts
content: A service account is a special type of Google account that belongs to your application or a VM, instead of an individual end user.
insight: Service accounts are both an 'identity' and a 'resource' that can have its own IAM policy.

title: Service Account Keys
content: Service account keys are used for authentication outside of Google Cloud. They are long-lived credentials that must be managed carefully.
insight: Avoid downloading keys; use Workload Identity or attach the SA directly to a VM instead.

lab.command: gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=my-app-sa@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com

title: Service Account Impersonation
content: Impersonation allows a user to act as a service account without needing its private key. This is more secure than using static keys.
insight: Requires the 'Service Account Token Creator' role on the target service account.

title: Workload Identity (GKE)
content: Workload Identity is the recommended way for your GKE workloads to access Google Cloud services by linking Kubernetes service accounts to GCP service accounts.
insight: Ensures that your containers only have the specific permissions they need, without managing secrets.

lab.command: echo 'Configure via GKE cluster and IAM policy bindings'
lab.output: Configure via GKE cluster and IAM policy bindings

title: Cloud KMS Overview
content: Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) is a managed service that allows you to create, use, rotate, and destroy cryptographic keys.
insight: Use KMS for encrypting sensitive data at rest using your own keys (CMEK).

title: Key Rings and Keys
content: A Key Ring is a logical grouping of Keys. Keys are used to perform cryptographic operations like encryption and decryption.
insight: Key Rings cannot be deleted, but individual Keys can be destroyed.

title: Envelope Encryption
content: Envelope encryption is the practice of encrypting data with a data encryption key (DEK) and then encrypting the DEK with a key encryption key (KEK).
insight: KMS is used to manage the KEK, while your application manages the DEK.

lab.command: echo 'KMS manages the KEK; the DEK encrypts the data'
lab.output: KMS manages the KEK; the DEK encrypts the data

title: Secret Manager Overview
content: Secret Manager is a secure and convenient storage system for sensitive information like API keys, passwords, and certificates.
insight: Provides versioning, audit logging, and fine-grained access control for secrets.

lab.output:
NAME      CREATED              REPLICATION_POLICY  LOCATIONS
db-pass   2023-10-10T10:00:00  automatic           -

title: Creating a Secret
content: You create a secret to hold sensitive data. Each secret can have multiple versions, allowing you to rotate credentials safely.
insight: Secret Manager handles replication and availability of your secrets globally or in specific regions.

title: Accessing a Secret
content: Users or service accounts need the 'Secret Manager Secret Accessor' role to retrieve the value of a secret version.
insight: Always reference secrets by version number or the 'latest' alias in your code.

title: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
content: IAP allows you to control access to your cloud applications and VMs based on user identity and context, without needing a VPN.
insight: IAP works by verifying the user's identity via Google accounts and then checking IAM policies.

title: IAP for TCP Forwarding
content: IAP can be used to provide secure SSH and RDP access to VMs that do not have external IP addresses.
insight: Eliminates the need for public IPs or bastion hosts for administrative access.

lab.output: Connecting to my-vm via IAP tunnel...

title: VPC Service Controls
content: VPC Service Controls allow you to define a security perimeter around your Google Cloud resources to mitigate data exfiltration risks.
insight: Ensures that data cannot be moved out of the perimeter to untrusted locations or projects.

lab.command: echo 'Create perimeters via Security -> VPC Service Controls'
lab.output: Create perimeters via Security -> VPC Service Controls

title: Cloud Armor Security Policies
content: Cloud Armor security policies allow you to filter traffic to your HTTP(S) load balancers based on IP addresses, geographic location, and custom expressions.
insight: Use Cloud Armor to protect your applications from DDoS attacks and common web vulnerabilities.

lab.command: gcloud compute security-policies create block-ips --description='Block malicious IPs'

title: Security Command Center (SCC)
content: SCC is a security and risk management platform that helps you discover, prevent, and detect threats in your Google Cloud environment.
insight: Provides a centralized dashboard for viewing security findings and compliance status.

lab.command: echo 'View findings in Security -> Security Command Center'
lab.output: View findings in Security -> Security Command Center

title: Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
content: Cloud DLP allows you to discover, classify, and protect sensitive data (like PII, credit card numbers) in your datasets and files.
insight: Use DLP to de-identify or mask sensitive data before sharing it with other teams or services.

lab.command: echo 'Create inspection jobs via Security -> Data Loss Prevention'
lab.output: Create inspection jobs via Security -> Data Loss Prevention

title: IAM Recommender
content: The IAM Recommender provides automated recommendations to help you apply the principle of least privilege by identifying over-privileged users.
insight: Review and apply recommendations regularly to reduce your project's attack surface.

title: Organization Policies
content: Organization policies give you centralized, programmatic control over your organization's resources, allowing you to restrict allowed configurations.
insight: Enforce policies like 'disable external IP addresses' or 'restrict allowed regions' globally.
next: Service Control Policies (SCPs) vs Org Policies

title: Resource Manager Organization
content: The Organization resource is the root node of the Google Cloud resource hierarchy. It allows for centralized management of all resources.
insight: Requires a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity account to create an Organization.

title: IAM Best Practices: Groups
content: Always manage access using Google Groups instead of granting roles to individual users. This makes team changes much easier to manage.
insight: Updating group membership automatically updates access for all group members across all projects.

lab.command: echo 'Add users to groups in the Google Admin Console'
lab.output: Add users to groups in the Google Admin Console

title: IAM Best Practices: Least Privilege
content: Grant only the minimum permissions required for a user or service account to perform its task. Avoid using basic roles (Owner/Editor) in production.
insight: Least privilege reduces the impact of compromised credentials.

lab.command: echo 'Use predefined or custom roles instead of basic roles'
lab.output: Use predefined or custom roles instead of basic roles

title: Cloud Identity Overview
content: Cloud Identity is an Identity as a Service (IDaaS) that helps you manage users and groups. It is the core authentication provider for GCP.
insight: Supports Single Sign-On (SSO) with third-party providers like Azure AD and Okta.

lab.command: echo 'Manage identities in Google Admin Console'
lab.output: Manage identities in Google Admin Console

title: Access Context Manager
content: Access Context Manager allows you to define fine-grained, attribute-based access control for projects and resources based on user identity and request context.
insight: Define 'access levels' based on IP range, device state, or user identity.

lab.output:
NAME                TITLE
corp-ip-only        Corporate IP Only

title: OS Login
content: OS Login allows you to use IAM roles to manage SSH access to your Compute Engine instances, instead of managing individual SSH keys.
insight: Provides centralized lifecycle management of SSH access for your team.

title: Binary Authorization Overview
content: Binary Authorization ensures that only trusted container images are deployed to GKE or Cloud Run by requiring signatures from authorized attestors.
insight: Prevents the deployment of unverified or malicious images in your production environment.

lab.command: echo 'Configure policies in Security -> Binary Authorization'
lab.output: Configure policies in Security -> Binary Authorization

title: Secret Rotation
content: Secret Manager supports automatic rotation of secrets by triggering a Cloud Function to update the credential in both the secret and the target service.
insight: Regularly rotating secrets reduces the window of opportunity for stolen credentials.

lab.command: echo 'Configure rotation period and Cloud Function in Secret settings'
lab.output: Configure rotation period and Cloud Function in Secret settings

title: Firewall Rules Logging
content: Firewall rules logging allows you to record connections that were allowed or denied by specific firewall rules.
insight: Use firewall logs to audit network traffic and identify potential security threats or misconfigurations.

title: Cloud KMS Key Rotation
content: You can configure Cloud KMS to automatically rotate encryption keys on a schedule. Each rotation creates a new key version.
insight: Automating key rotation helps comply with security standards and best practices.

title: Access Approval
content: Access Approval ensures that Google personnel must have your explicit approval before they can access your data or configurations for troubleshooting.
insight: Adds an extra layer of control over your data, ensuring that access only happens when you request it.

title: Security Health Analytics
content: Security Health Analytics (part of SCC) automatically scans your GCP environment for misconfigurations and security vulnerabilities.
insight: Detects issues like public buckets, open firewall ports, and missing audit logs.

title: BeyondCorp Enterprise
content: BeyondCorp is Google's implementation of zero-trust security. It ensures that every request is authenticated and authorized based on device and user context.
insight: Moves security from the network perimeter to individual users and devices.

lab.command: echo 'Integrated with IAP and Access Context Manager'
lab.output: Integrated with IAP and Access Context Manager

title: Cloud IDS
content: Cloud Intrusion Detection System (IDS) provides managed network security that detects malware, spyware, and command-and-control attacks.
insight: Uses Palo Alto Networks technology to inspect mirrored traffic in your VPC.

lab.output:

title: Troubleshooting IAM Policies
content: Use the IAM Policy Troubleshooter to analyze why a user has or doesn't have a specific permission on a resource.
insight: Accounts for role inheritance, conditions, and service-specific permissions.

lab.command: echo 'Access via IAM -> Policy Troubleshooter in the Console'
lab.output: Access via IAM -> Policy Troubleshooter in the Console

title: Shielded VM Security
content: Shielded VMs provide verifiable integrity of your VM instances using features like Secure Boot and Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM).
insight: Protects against boot-level and kernel-level rootkits and malware.

title: Conclusion: Security on GCP
content: You have learned the core tools and best practices for securing your Google Cloud environment, from IAM to encryption and threat detection.
insight: Security is an ongoing process of monitoring, hardening, and adapting to new threats.
